_readme: GROUND TRUTH for control.lts. HAND-AUTHORED. Parsed by `json`, NEVER by the system
under test.
WHY A SIDECAR AND NOT THE CORPUS. Two independent reasons, both load-bearing:
1. CORRELATED CORRUPTION. If the expectations lived inside control.lts they would be
read by the very parser being tested. A parser broken enough to misread the corpus
would misread its own oracle, and the check would agree with itself. The oracle must
be read by a DIFFERENT reader (`json`) than the one under test.
2. THE INPUT MUST NOT MOVE WHEN THE EXPECTATION DOES. Expectations legitimately change
over time -- a silent-loss class is added, a severity is promoted, a count shifts.
A sidecar makes that a reviewable DATA diff. Editing the corpus to change an
expectation would perturb the thing being measured in the same commit that changes
the measurement.
STOP -- DO NOT REGENERATE THIS FILE FROM PARSER OUTPUT.
There is deliberately NO --update-expectations / --regenerate / --bless flag, and no
helper anywhere in this repo that writes this file. Not for convenience, not for a
one-off. The reason is mechanical, not stylistic: if a red self-check can be made green
by re-recording actual output, then the cheap move on every failure is to re-record, the
bug becomes the expectation, and from that moment the control CAN ONLY EVER PASS. A
control that cannot fail is not a control -- it is a green light wired to the ignition.
If you are here because the self-check went red: the parser is the suspect, not this
file. Change this file only as a deliberate, reviewed diff that carries a REASON in its
commit message -- the same discipline DELIBERATELY_UNMAPPED carries in
tools/tests/test_gate_reachability.py, where adding an entry is a
decision that a diff surfaces to a reviewer.
THE RECORD IS TWO-LEVEL, and the levels are NOT 1:1.
LEVEL 1 (primary) -- `lines`: one declared disposition per SOURCE LINE, which is exactly
what SPEC 2.5 already models (every non-blank line is CONSUMED by a parser branch or
CLASSIFIED as one of 2.3's ignorable forms). The parser already produces this record
in LineCoverage; we compare against it directly rather than inventing a second
accounting. This is what makes a failure NAME itself: 'line 109 should have been
FLAGGED as a capitalised key, the parser CONSUMED it as a property' localises the
defect, where 'expected 12 properties, got 11' only starts an investigation.
LEVEL 2 -- `graph`: the artifacts (nodes, their exact properties, findings, counts).
THE BRIDGE -- each line's `contributes` names the graph artifact(s) that line produced.
The mapping is deliberately NOT flattened into a line->artifact table, because it is
not a function in either direction: a P5 mapping is SEVERAL lines producing ONE
property; a P3 multi-value line is ONE line producing SEVERAL edges; a heading is ONE
line producing a node AND its CONTAINS edge AND all of its property-inferred edges
(the parser attributes E4 edges to the node's HEADING line, not to the property line
-- recorded here as fact, since it is the parser's real behaviour).
TOTALITY. Every one of the 200 lines belongs to exactly one case, and every node belongs
to exactly one case. The runner asserts that partition before it checks anything, so a
line cannot be quietly dropped from the oracle to make a failure disappear.
ORACLE v2 (2026-08-11) -- FIVE cases and 33 lines ADDED, none changed. The control had
neither a WRAPPED property value nor an ID TABLE among its live shapes, and both
classes were bleeding in the corpora while all 24 cases passed: 41-example-wrapped-
values.lts captured 23% of its authored bytes, and its `[ACME-SUB-ACCEPT]`
-- a 14-row acceptance contract -- captured 7%. A control cannot measure a class it
does not contain, so the classes were added as LIVE SHAPES (SL-19 wrapped value, SL-20
ID table) with an EXCLUSION beside each: an indented BULLET that must not be folded
(line 168) and a decorative table that must not be promoted (lines 179-182). The
pre-existing lines 1-155 and their dispositions are BYTE-IDENTICAL; the only edited
expectations are CTRL-DOC.properties (it now owns the ancestor-attached table at line
188) and the GRAPH-TOTALS counts.
ORACLE v3 (2026-08-11) -- FOUR cases and 12 lines ADDED, none changed. Same story as v2,
one grammar over: the control contained no property-shaped bullet whose KEY REGION
carried a qualifier, so SL-21 (parenthetical) and SL-22 (en/em-dash) bled through 27
green cases. Measured on the day they were named: 163 occurrences across the Acme
corpora, 151 parenthetical and 12 dashed, in 21 files -- and FOUR of them inside
tests/fixtures/preview/spec29-clean-control.lts, the file whose entire job was to be
the CLEAN negative control. `lts_preview` reported it at 100.0% coverage, 0 lost.
Both classes are added as LIVE SHAPES with an EXCLUSION BESIDE EACH, one line below its
positive and inside the same node: line 193 puts the parenthesis in the VALUE and line
199 puts an em-dash AND a later colon in the VALUE. Both must keep PARSING.
WHAT THE EXCLUSIONS DISCRIMINATE, measured by mutation rather than asserted: widening
`_PROP_SIMPLE_RE`'s key to a greedy `[a-z].*` -- the 'just parse the qualified form'
fix the ruling forbids -- turns BOTH exclusions red (the key boundary moves to the LAST
colon and each value is destroyed) at the same time as it turns both positives red.
WHAT THEY DO NOT DISCRIMINATE, recorded so the claim is not over-sold: an over-eager
COVERAGE CLASSIFIER. `classify_line` returns KIND_CONSUMED before the near-miss check,
so an unanchored variant of both new regexes leaves this control 33/33 GREEN. The
exclusions guard the parser's key boundary, not the classifier's precision; the
classifier's precision is guarded by the corpus measurement, not by this file.
The pre-existing lines 1-188 and their
dispositions are BYTE-IDENTICAL; the only edited expectations are the GRAPH-TOTALS
counts and WRAPPED-VALUE-EXCLUSION's flagged_line_count (3 -> 5), both mechanical
consequences of the appended lines.
ORACLE v4 (2026-08-15, RECORDED RETROSPECTIVELY) -- FIVE cases and 21 lines were added
by 3f9a2c1 for the property-KEY minting classes SL-24..SL-28 (`relates-to` mapped to
nothing across 140 occurrences while this control was GREEN at 34/34). That commit
updated CONTROL_DIGEST correctly but left BOTH provenance fields stale: no v4 note
here, and `measured_against` still claiming `SL-1 .. SL-23`. The consequence is
narrow but is exactly the failure this artifact exists to prevent -- `measured_against`
is returned VERBATIM in every lts_selfcheck verdict, so a green run was reporting the
wrong class list, and standing rule 4 ('a cleanliness claim carries the class list and
the date it was measured against') was mechanically false. Repaired in the same commit
that adds v5, and recorded rather than silently corrected.
ORACLE v5 (2026-08-15) -- FOUR cases ADDED, ZERO lines added, none changed. This is the
first oracle change that adds NO source lines: SL-29..SL-32 carry empty `lines` and
empty `nodes` because their subject is the PROFILE LOADER, not control.lts. The damage
they measure happens at profile LOAD, before any document is read -- a stale process
carrying the pre-guard loader parses control.lts perfectly and will STILL accept a
profile that shadows core PART_OF, after which every layer-scoped traversal in the
deployment silently returns a subset. Because no line was added, every pre-existing
line disposition, every node and every GRAPH-TOTALS count is BYTE-IDENTICAL, and
control.lts itself is UNTOUCHED (301 inserted lines, 0 deleted, all in this file).
THE COMPROMISE, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. These cases carry `given_profile` /
`given_profiles`, which are INPUTS living in a file that is supposed to hold ground
truth only. The rule that exists to protect is CORRELATED CORRUPTION: an oracle read
by the system under test would be misread by the same defect and the check would agree
with itself. That risk is structurally ABSENT here, because `load_profile(dict)` never
touches the .lts parser -- fixture and expectation share no reader. The input keys are
named `given_*` so an input can never be mistaken for an expectation.
EVERY REFUSAL CASE IS PAIRED WITH AN ACCEPTANCE. SL-32 exists solely so that a loader
which refused EVERYTHING could not score green on SL-29..SL-31, and `error_contains`
exists so that a refusal saying only 'invalid profile' cannot satisfy a rule whose
content is 'refuse, NAMING BOTH DEFINITIONS'.
WHAT A GREEN RESULT DOES NOT MEAN. See the module docstring of
factlattice_engine/selfcheck.py. This measures recall against a KNOWN class list only.
ORACLE v6 (2026-08-16, Era 1 RATIFY) -- SEVEN cases ADDED, ZERO lines added, none
changed. control.lts is UNTOUCHED; every pre-existing line disposition, node and
GRAPH-TOTALS count is BYTE-IDENTICAL. These carry empty `lines`/`nodes` for the
SL-29..SL-32 reason generalised: their subject is not a region of control.lts.
For SL-37 the subject is the ENTRY POINT (no document expresses it). For
SL-34..SL-36 the subject is the document's MODE, and the reason is structural
rather than convenient: every one of these classes compares THE SAME BYTES under
TWO configurations (legacy vs strict; verb registered vs not; key declared vs
not). control.lts is one file with one absent marker parsed under one core-only
config, so it can hold ONE ARM of each pair and never both -- a two-mode
comparison is not expressible as a region of a single corpus file.
THE CORRELATED-CORRUPTION RULE IS INTACT, and it is worth restating because
these cases carry `given_document` -- .lts text read by the parser under test.
The rule protects EXPECTATIONS, not inputs: control.lts has always been an input
read by the parser while its oracle was read by `json`, and `given_document` is
the same arrangement inline. Every expectation beside it (`mode`, `kinds`,
`severity`, `suggestions`) is still read by `json` and never by the parser, and
inputs are named `given_*` so one can never be mistaken for the other.
EVERY NEW CASE IS PAIRED. A regime check that can only fire is as useless as one
that can only pass: ERA1-KEY-PROFILE-DECLARED exists so a check that flagged
every non-core key cannot score green on ERA1-KEY-DECLARED-OR-MARKED;
ERA1-VERB-PROSE-TARGET's second arm registers the verb and demands the finding
DISAPPEAR; ERA1-ENTRY-POINT-EQUIVALENCE carries `negative_control: true`, which
starves one path and requires the instrument to notice.
measured_against: silent-loss-classes v10 (2026-10-07), SL-1 .. SL-40 -- SL-23 is the first SUBSTITUTION class (every other class up to it makes something DISAPPEAR; SL-23 makes something LIE); SL-24..SL-28 are the property-KEY minting classes; SL-29..SL-32 are the EDGE-TYPE NAMESPACE classes and are the first cases here whose subject is the PROFILE LOADER rather than the document parser; SL-33 is the MALFORMED-REF class (Era 0 / PARSER-ENGINEERING-SPEC.md rev 2 C1, SPEC A4): a bracket that is id-SHAPED but not a well-formed id, at a ref-expecting position, is now a `malformed_ref` finding instead of silence; SL-34..SL-37 are the ERA 1 RATIFICATION classes and are the first cases whose subject is the document's MODE rather than its bytes -- SL-34 the format-version marker (absence=legacy, presence=strict, and the GRAPH identical across both), SL-35 the A2 declared-or-marked key regime (core / profile-declared / x-marked / undeclared, with edit-distance suggestion), SL-36 the A3 verb regime including the prose-target path that was silent and unspecified, SL-37 entry-point equivalence (the V5/V5b/V5c wiring, green as of C3/C4 and guarded by its own negative control); SL-39 is the review-extension EDGE class (2026-10-07): `attaches-to-hook` (REVPROC -> REVHOOK) and `applies-rule` (REVPROC -> REVRULE, REVRULE -> existing rule) mint forward edges, `order` stays a property, and the look-alikes `applies-to` / `attaches-to` mint nothing (SL-39b); SL-38 is the `canonical-node` minting class (2026-10-03): a legacy node pointing at its canonical node, a FORWARD CANONICAL edge that is NOT supersession; SL-38b pins that BARE `canonical` (free-text status prose on 10 live nodes) mints nothing; SL-40 is the REVIEW-SHAPE class (2026-10-07, A-E4): a review or extension node must carry its required properties and declare its keys under the shipped reviewer profile, judged by counting V3 findings because every profile finding is a warning, with a stripped twin so that an emptied required list is visible; its subject is the reviewer PROFILE, not the document parser

findings._note: this one was ALREADY here before SL-33 was added: `not-an-id` is a single, all-lowercase, hyphenated token, which the literal A4 grammar classifies MALFORMED-REF (identifier-shaped, not well-formed, carries a dash) even with no upper-initial. LOWERCASE-BRACKET-IS-PROSE's own edge-minting assertion is UNCHANGED (still no RELATED_TO edge) -- only a diagnostic was added, per Era 0's own compatibility contract.

114._note: SL-13 is a KNOWN-SILENT class in silent-loss-classes v4 (detected: NO). An en-dash is not a Markdown bullet, so the coverage classifier's _BULLET_RE never matches and the line reads as prose. The control pins the ACTUAL behaviour -- the property is NOT set (that is the SL-13 assertion) and the line is NOT flagged (that is the recorded gap). Promoting this to FLAGGED is a parser/classifier change plus a class-list version bump, not an oracle edit.

119._note: SL-14 is a KNOWN-SILENT class in silent-loss-classes v4 (detected: NO). _KEY_COLON_RE requires whitespace after the colon -- the requirement that keeps https:// and doc:// URIs out of the finding set -- so `- owner:selfcheck` is not even near-miss-shaped. Same discipline as line 114: the property being ABSENT is the assertion; the line being unflagged is the recorded gap.

124._note: TWO independent alarms for one shape, both required: the parser raises a mixed_property_block FINDING, and because it consumes NO line the coverage lint ALSO reports the head. Either alarm alone would be a single point of failure.

131._note: The line IS consumed and the property IS set to the literal text. What must not happen is an EDGE: [not-an-id] fails _UPPER_ID_RE, so it is prose in brackets, and see-also mints nothing from it. Note the heading (line 129) therefore carries NO RELATED_TO edge.

142._note: THE DISCRIMINATING EXCLUSION LINE. Lines 139-141 are indented and would classify as prose/nested_list_prose anywhere. Line 142 is a COLUMN-0 `- key: value` bullet -- the exact shape that fires near_miss_property everywhere else in this file (see lines 104/109). It is prose ONLY because classify_line short-circuits inside a `## Relationships` section. Delete that short-circuit and this line, and only this line, turns red. That is what makes the exclusion measurable rather than vacuous.

147._note: SL-18. The declared type is the WHOLE dotted token. The bare suffix is deliberately a CORE verb (DEPENDS_ON): with a non-core suffix a tokenizer regression would make the edge VANISH, which line accounting already catches. With a core suffix the regression instead SUBSTITUTES a bare, unflagged DEPENDS_ON that line accounting is structurally blind to -- which is the actual SL-18 defect, and the thing this case exists to catch.

148._note: SL-11. ONE edge, carrying the AUTHORED verb and the WHOLE target id. The target id contains the core verb SUPERSEDES as a substring; the positional token scan would match it and emit an edge to the literal string '-55]'. The anchored `[SRC] VERB [` form must win first. The line-level record cannot express 'and nothing else', so the case also carries no_edge_matching assertions.

168._note: THE WRAP EXCLUSION LINE. Indented deeper than its `- note:` head, non-blank, immediately below a continuation line that WAS folded (167) -- every property of a continuation except one: it opens with a bullet. A fold rule that reached one column further would swallow this line and, worse, would swallow the P4 sub-list idiom everywhere in the corpora. It is the only line in this file that is indented, adjacent to a folded value, and still ignorable.

181._note: THE TABLE DISCRIMINATION LINE. Byte-for-byte the same SHAPE as line 174 -- a `|`-delimited row inside an `[ID]`-bearing node body, under a header and a rule. It is ignorable for exactly one structural reason: its first column is not an identifier column (header `Layer`, cells `narrative`/`grid`). Loosen the discriminator and this line, and lines 179/180/182, turn into properties on CASE-PLAIN-TABLE. That is what makes the exclusion measurable rather than asserted.

192._note: SL-21. FLAGGED, and DELIBERATELY NOT PARSED. `requirement (qualified)` is genuinely ambiguous -- the key could be `requirement` or `requirement (qualified)` -- and accepting it means GUESSING. A guessed key is a SUBSTITUTION, which SL-18 established is worse than a loss: a missing property is detectable, a plausible wrong one is not. The paired assertion is no_property_anywhere, which is what proves the parser did not quietly pick one.

193._note: THE PAREN DISCRIMINATION LINE, one line below its positive and in the same node. It carries TWO parentheticals and a SECOND COLON, and it PARSES -- because all of that is in the VALUE, after the FIRST colon. MEASURED, so the claim is not folklore: widen `_PROP_SIMPLE_RE`'s key to a greedy `[a-z].*` (the 'just accept the qualified form' fix the ruling forbids) and the split lands on the LAST colon -- this node's property becomes `delta: (leading paren in value) form (measured)` and the assertion names the damage. ⛔ WHAT THIS LINE DOES *NOT* CATCH, also measured: an over-eager COVERAGE CLASSIFIER. `classify_line` returns KIND_CONSUMED before it ever reaches the near-miss check, so a classifier regex that searched the whole line instead of the key region leaves the control 33/33 GREEN. The exclusion pins the KEY-BOUNDARY rule in the PARSER, which is where the ruling's 'do not guess the key' actually lives; it is not a guard on the classifier's precision.

198._note: SL-22. Same ruling and same reasoning as line 192, DIFFERENT KIND -- the two are kept apart because their incidences are measured apart (151 parenthetical vs 12 dashed across the Acme corpora on the day they were named). Note this is NOT SL-13: there the en-dash IS the bullet marker and `_BULLET_RE` never matches; here the bullet is a proper hyphen and the dash sits inside the key region.

199._note: THE DASH DISCRIMINATION LINE, and the same measured story as line 193 in the dash spelling: an em-dash AND a colon after it, both inside the VALUE, and the line PARSES. Under the greedy-key mutation this node's property becomes `boundary: an em-dash inside a value — and a colon after it`. Same caveat as 193: it does not catch an over-eager classifier, because a consumed line never reaches the classifier's near-miss branch.

202._note: SL-23. ⛔ THE LINE IS FULLY CONSUMED AND FULLY WRONG. Line accounting is GREEN here, the key-loss rule sees nothing (no bullet), and `lts_lint` reported no diagnostic of any kind on this shape before the id-hijack rule existed — because nothing was LOST. A node was minted, it parses, it is queryable, and it is the WRONG NODE. Every other class in this control makes something DISAPPEAR; this one makes something LIE, which is why it needed its own case and could not be folded into a coverage or key-region assertion.

204._note: And the substitution's second half: this property is attributed to the CITATION, not to the node the author declared. In the live shape — where the cited id is also defined elsewhere — the two collide and first-root-wins drops one section out of the graph entirely.

206._note: ⛔ EDGE PROVENANCE IS THE HEADING LINE, NOT THE PROPERTY LINE. The E4 minter stamps `source_line` from the node's HEADING, so a property edge is attributed here rather than to the `- key: value` that authored it. Recorded because the oracle was written the other way round and this control caught it — the same line-attribution assumption would misplace any future per-line edge report.

208._note: SL-24. The defect that opened the 2026-08-15 work: `relates-to` is the natural spelling of RELATED_TO and appeared 140 times across 11 files in the acme corpora, minting NOTHING, while `lts_lint` reported every one of those files CLEAN and `lts_selfcheck` returned PASS 34/34 with a matching digest. The class was not on the list, so the control was green and the graph was wrong.

210._note: ⛔ EDGE PROVENANCE IS THE HEADING LINE, NOT THE PROPERTY LINE. The E4 minter stamps `source_line` from the node's HEADING, so a property edge is attributed here rather than to the `- key: value` that authored it. Recorded because the oracle was written the other way round and this control caught it — the same line-attribution assumption would misplace any future per-line edge report.

212._note: SL-25. ⛔ REVERSED. The edge runs referenced_id -> node, so the SOURCE is CASE-P1-SIMPLE. A direction error here would be a SUBSTITUTION, not a loss: the graph would answer supersession traversals confidently and backwards.

214._note: ⛔ EDGE PROVENANCE IS THE HEADING LINE, NOT THE PROPERTY LINE. The E4 minter stamps `source_line` from the node's HEADING, so a property edge is attributed here rather than to the `- key: value` that authored it. Recorded because the oracle was written the other way round and this control caught it — the same line-attribution assumption would misplace any future per-line edge report.

216._note: SL-26. ⛔ REVERSED. `verify` had 35 pure uses in the live corpora while `tested-by` — the official spelling of the same edge — had ZERO. The expressive name is the one an author reaches for.

218._note: ⛔ EDGE PROVENANCE IS THE HEADING LINE, NOT THE PROPERTY LINE. The E4 minter stamps `source_line` from the node's HEADING, so a property edge is attributed here rather than to the `- key: value` that authored it. Recorded because the oracle was written the other way round and this control caught it — the same line-attribution assumption would misplace any future per-line edge report.

220._note: SL-27. An insight SPAWNS a decision — the core causal CAUSES, forward.

224._note: SL-28. ⛔ THE ANTI-OVER-REACH CONTROL, and it is as load-bearing as the four above. `rationale` carries a bracketed id INSIDE A SENTENCE. Measured over the acme corpora, `rationale` (96 occurrences), `definition` (94) and `requirement` (58) are 0% pure reference lists. This line MUST mint no edge: a table that harvested every bracketed id would turn every inline citation into a graph edge and destroy what a traversal means. `contributes` carries the property and NO edge, so a regression in either direction fails here.

229._note: SL-33. The line IS consumed and `relates-to` IS set to the literal text `[Mixed-Case-Attempt]`. `relates-to` MINTS (a built-in RELATED_TO key since 2026-08-15) but this bracket fails `_UPPER_ID_RE` (mixed case), so `_property_refs` extracts zero refs and no edge is minted -- exactly the CASE-LOWER-BRACKET pattern one case over. What's NEW: the bracket is bracket-SHAPED like an ATTEMPTED id (an upper-initial plus dashes, unlike `not-an-id`'s all-lowercase shape), so `classify_bracket_token` calls it MALFORMED-REF rather than PROSE-BRACKET, and the parser now raises `ParseFinding(kind='malformed_ref')` for it (SPEC A4 / C1).
